newsitem.title: UK: Cathay may axe ex-UK cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Cathay may axe ex-UK cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd UK cargo managers will meet over the next few days to discuss lifting a fuel surcharge imposed last November 25, said north UK cargo manager Ivor Llewellyn.

"Although no firm decision has yet been taken, my gut feeling is that we will recommend to our Hong Kong head office that the five pence per kg surcharge should be withdrawn from May 1," he told Reuters.
Cathay, along with most other airlines, introduced surcharges to counter rapidly increasing fuel costs.
A number of airlines now feel that the price of jet fuel has dropped to a level that does not require any surcharges.
Three carriers -- Delta Air Lines, Virgin Atlantic and United Airlines -- have already announced they are dropping their fuel-related cargo surcharges.

Llewellyn said that because of varying market conditions and government regulations applicable in different countries, each Cathay overseas cargo station had responsibility for recommending its own fuel surcharge policies.

He said that Cathay's attitude on the future of ex-UK fuel surcharges was not influenced by that of national carrier British Airways, which has yet to make a decision on whether or not to lift its own surcharges.
